elements.texte:
[cheerful] The warehouse dashboard must show an alert for each product.

Under 50 in stock: Reorder. Under 100: Watch. Otherwise: OK.

For this, we get the name and stock of the 8 products in the products table.

The alert, though, isn’t stored anywhere: we have to calculate it.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] That’s the job of case: choosing a value based on conditions.

The when part gives the condition, and the then part, the value to show if it’s true.

Else gives the value for all other cases, and end closes the case.

Let’s take Omega 3, with 90 in stock: 90 less than 50 is false.

The second condition, 90 less than 100, is true.

Case so keeps the matching result: “Watch”.

The conditions are tested one by one, from top to bottom: after the first true one, the rest is ignored.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Watch the order: in this case, stock less than 100 is tested first.

The Steel Shaker has 30 in stock: 30 less than 100 is true, so it gets “Watch”.

Stock less than 50 is never reached: no product gets “Reorder”.

The strictest condition must come first: stock less than 50 first.
